name: Cainan
overview: Cainan is a male figure mentioned in the lineage of the Messiah, as noted in Luke 3:36. He is sometimes spelled Kenan or Kainan in various English Bible texts. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he holds significance as an ancestor within the godly line leading to Christ.
namesAndTitles: The name Cainan appears as a proper name in Luke 3:36 without a specified meaning or divine origin. The variations Kenan or Kainan reflect different transliterations in English Bible versions but do not add further meaning beyond the proper name itself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Cainan beyond what is indicated in his inclusion in the Messianic genealogy. No additional relational details are provided in the given facts.
scriptureSignificance: Cainan is important as a link in the sacred lineage that connects the antediluvian patriarchs to Noah, Abraham, and ultimately the Messiah. His place in this genealogy underscores the preservation of godly heritage and the continuation of God's redemptive plan through successive generations before the flood.
